finding.claim: statement_timeout= stores the configured ms in ctx->stmt_timeout but the progress handler never reads it, so queries are interrupted after roughly 1000-2000 VM ops regardless of the configured value; prepared statements reused via reset!/step are interrupted on their second run because the deadline is only cleared in prepare. Logic error, availability impact only, fail-closed (no security bypass).
finding.sink: sqlite3_progress_handler registration at ext/sqlite3/database.c:443-445, callback rb_sqlite3_statement_timeout at ext/sqlite3/database.c:412-427 returning 1 (SQLITE_INTERRUPT)

trace.note: n = 0 ? -1 : 1000; ms value not used for the deadline
first callback: if deadline unset, deadline = now
later callback: if now after deadline, return 1 (interrupt)
deadline cleared only in prepare; reset!/step reuse keeps stale deadline (statement.c:318-332)

finding.guards_checked: ctx->stmt_timeout is written (database.c:442) and grep shows no read anywhere in ext/sqlite3; the progress handler (database.c:412-427) has no reference to the configured value; no reset of stmt_deadline outside prepare (statement.c:82). No enforced control makes the timeout match the configured ms.

finding.claim: Ruby callbacks invoked from SQLite C code without rb_protect (authorizer, collation comparator, busy handler, trace) let a Ruby exception longjmp through SQLite internals, skipping SQLite cleanup and potentially leaving the connection in an inconsistent state or holding its mutex. Sibling callbacks rb_sqlite3_func and the aggregator do wrap calls in rb_protect. PLAUSIBLE: consequence inside SQLite is inferred, since SQLite source is not in this tree; precondition is an application-supplied callback that raises on attacker-influenced input.
finding.source: SQL text supplied to the library, passed to the authorizer's table/column arguments at ext/sqlite3/database.c:733-737 (via Statement#prepare at ext/sqlite3/statement.c:70)
finding.sink: rb_funcall(db_ctx->authorizer, "call", ...) at ext/sqlite3/database.c:738 (unprotected); similar unprotected calls at database.c:328 (tracefunc), 365 (busy handler), 839 (rb_comparator_func, with NUM2INT at 841)

trace.note: rb_funcall invokes Ruby authorizer with no rb_protect; a raised exception longjmps out of sqlite3_prepare_v2
sibling rb_sqlite3_func wraps its call in rb_protect (contrast)
sibling aggregator wraps its call in rb_protect (contrast)

finding.guards_checked: rb_protect present for define_function (database.c:581) and aggregator (aggregator.c:47) but absent for rb_sqlite3_auth (database.c:738), rb_comparator_func (database.c:839), rb_sqlite3_busy_handler (database.c:365), tracefunc (database.c:328). Return-value handling (database.c:740-744) does not catch exceptions. No rb_protect or rb_rescue wraps these calls.
